ideas_declared.rationale: note p.4 'Ideal Entry setup', encoded EXACTLY as written: '20EMA > 50SMA > 10EMA > 200MA'. This ordering is internally odd (10EMA sits below 50SMA while the setup is described as a 'strong intermediate trend'); tested verbatim on purpose, see stacked_alignment_conventional for the alternative reading. Exit uses the note's own timing signal, '5EMA crossing 20EMA', in its bearish direction.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline

ideas_declared.entry: ema(10) > ema(20) and ema(20) > sma(50) and sma(50) > sma(200)
ideas_declared.rationale: The conventional 'stacked moving averages' reading of the same note passage: fastest on top, slowest on bottom (ema(10) > ema(20) > sma(50) > sma(200)), i.e. what most technical-analysis literature means by 'aligned uptrend'. Tested as a separate idea from ideal_entry_verbatim so the data can say which reading it prefers.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
ideas_declared.source: note p.4 'Ideal Entry setup' (conventional stacked-alignment reading)

ideas_declared.rationale: note p.9 'MA Strategy' page: entry = long-term MA120/200 direction aligned with price location (encoded as price above both the 120 and 200 SMA, since MA slope is not expressible in this DSL) plus a MA5-MA20 crossover in the long-term direction; exit = BB(20,2) band touch OR a MA5-MA8/20 crossover (encoded as MA5 x MA20, since two independent fast MAs (8 and 20) both mapping to 'the fast leg' is ambiguous -- 20 was chosen to match the entry leg).
